doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Mastering problems and logging take numbers on Billy May's date
summary: Hank answers about mastering changing a record, then describes the second engineer's stress at a Billy May session and noting take start numbers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Was it an odd feeling or did you ever have the circumstance where you spent a great deal of time on a recording and it was done and then only to be ruined or changed in the mastering process?

That’s happened a few times. Generally — I don’t know how to put this — sometimes the guy in the cutting room is hearing something that you didn’t hear. You know? And he’ll ask you, “Gee you guys made a cut here but it doesn’t sound right.” No that’s wrong too, I mean at that point if the guy says that you get nervous. But sometimes the guys in the cutting room will catch something and say hey, this doesn’t sound right, what did you do. And you know I don’t know how that worked because I never made any major mistakes, knock on wood thank God.

The worst part of a job in a big studio for a second engineer was to be in the middle of a date, you’re doing — Billy May’s out there with a big band, you’ve got a hot producer, you’ve got a hot engineer, and they turn around and say, “I like the first chorus of track 12 and I put it together with the track of 18” or whatever. They’re all starting to talk and you’re trying to find what take it is. You know? That’s when you get into — it gets crazy. And I always talk like a second engineer because I’ve been it myself. I would write down the start of the take by numbers, I could see that on the machine. You know? And then I knew that that’s where the start was, 82 or whatever. And, “Let’s get to the third take,” I knew where that was I’d just reel the tape up, instead of trying to hunt for where it started. I wrote down the number. I knew that it started at 82, I’d go to 82 and there’s the start of it. I always used to write them on the box.
